** Question: What is the association of alcohol consumption and CKD, and does sex modify this association? Smoking is a known risk factor for CKD, but does sex modify this as well? **

```{r}

library(caret)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(tidyverse)
library(randomForest)
library(dplyr)
library(ranger)
library(pROC)
library(ggplot2)
library(pdp)
library(MASS)

set.seed(123)

ckd_filter <- readRDS("shared_df_filter.rds")

ckd_filter$Beer <- factor(
  as.character(ckd_filter$Low_alcohol_beer) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Mid_strength_beer) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Full_strength_beer) == "1",
  levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  labels = c("0", "1")
)

ckd_filter$Wine <- factor(
  as.character(ckd_filter$White_wine) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Red_wine) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Low_alcohol_wine) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Champagne_sparkling_wine) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Fortified_wine) == "1",
  levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  labels = c("0", "1")
)

ckd_filter$Spirits_Liqueurs <- factor(
  as.character(ckd_filter$Spirits_RTD) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Liqueurs) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Spirits) == "1",
  levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  labels = c("0", "1")
)

ckd_filter$Other <- factor(
  as.character(ckd_filter$Cider) == "1" |
  as.character(ckd_filter$Cocktails) == "1",
  levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
  labels = c("0", "1")
)

bev_cols <- c("Low_alcohol_beer","Mid_strength_beer","Full_strength_beer",
              "White_wine","Red_wine","Low_alcohol_wine",
              "Champagne_sparkling_wine","Spirits_RTD","Liqueurs",
              "Spirits","Fortified_wine","Cider","Cocktails")

ckd_filter <- ckd_filter %>%
  dplyr::select(-SEX, -Alcohol_risk, -smoker_status, -daily_smoke, -Alcohol_risk_7day) 

table(train$CKD) / nrow(train)   # check class imbalance

#Need to fix class imbalance

idx   <- sample(nrow(ckd_filter), 0.7 * nrow(ckd_filter))
train <- rf_data[idx, ]
test  <- rf_data[-idx, ]

train_maj <- train %>% filter(CKD == "0")
train_min <- train %>% filter(CKD == "1")


train_up <- bind_rows(
  train_maj,
  train_min[sample(nrow(train_min), nrow(train_maj), replace = TRUE), ]
)

table(train_up$CKD)   # should now be balanced

rf <- randomForest(CKD ~ .,
                  data = train_up,
                  ntree = 500,
                  importance = TRUE,
 )

rf

# Evaluate on the untouched test set
pred_class <- predict(rf, test)
pred_prob  <- predict(rf, test, type = "prob")[, "1"]

table(Predicted = pred_class, Actual = test$CKD)
auc(roc(test$CKD, pred_prob))


tree <- rpart(CKD ~ ., data = train_up, method = "class",
              control = rpart.control(cp = 0.005, minbucket = 30))

```

mda_scores <- importance(rf, type = 1, scale = FALSE)



Predicted CKD risk across alcohol quantity levels, were viewed separately by sex. A 2-way partial dependence plot of alcohol quantity and sex was mapped simultaneously against the variable CKD.

```{r}

pd <- partial(rf, pred.var = c("SEX_factor", "alcohol_quantity"), grid.resolution = 40, chull = TRUE)

autoplot(pd, contour = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "2D Partial Dependence Plot for Random Forest",
       x = "Sex",
       y = "Alcohol quantity in last week",
       fill = "Partial\nDependence") +
  theme_minimal()

pd <- partial(rf, pred.var = c("SEX_factor", "Alcohol_risk_7day"), grid.resolution = 40, chull = TRUE)

autoplot(pd, contour = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "2D Partial Dependence Plot for Random Forest",
       x = "Sex",
       y = "7-day Alcohol risk ",
       fill = "Partial\nDependence") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The effect of alcohol quantity changes, depending on sex. This does indicate an interaction effect between sex and alcohol consumption on CKD. However this is not a formal hypothesis test. 

```{r}
#Plot with highly-aesthetic arguments
rpart.plot(tree, 
           type = 2,               # Split labels below the nodes
           extra = 104,            # Displays class, probabilities, and % of obs
           shadow.col = "gray",    # Subtle drop shadow under boxes
           nn = TRUE,              # Display node numbers
           faclen = 0)              

ts_class_err <- 1 - confusionMatrix(rf_data$CKD,
                                    predict(rf,
                                    newdata=rf_data,
                                    type="class"))$byClass["Recall"]

ts_class_err[1:2]

# MeanDecreaseAccuracy = permutation importance

options(digits=2)
rf$importance[,1:4]
varImpPlot(rf) #Shows what variables contributed most to the random forest

#Vote matrix
rf$votes

```
```{r}

# 1. Extract importance values
imp_data <- as.data.frame((randomForest::importance(rf))) 

rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "AGE"] <- "Age"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "alcohol_quantity" ] <- "Alcohol Quantity"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "SEX_factor" ] <- "Sex"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Red_wine" ] <- "Red Wine"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "White_wine" ] <- "White Wine"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Full_strength_beer"] <- "Full Strength Beer"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Alcohol_risk_7day"] <- "7 day Alcohol Risk"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Champagne_sparkling_wine"] <- "Champagne/Sparkling Wine"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Mid_strength_beer"] <- "Mid Strength Beer"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Spirits_RTD"] <- "Ready to Drink Spirits"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Low_alcohol_beer"] <- "Low Alcohol Beer"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Fortified_wine"] <- "Fortified Wine"
rownames(imp_data)[rownames(imp_data) == "Low_alcohol_wine"] <- "Low alcohol wine"


imp_data$Variable <- rownames(imp_data)

#rownames(imp_data) <- c("", "", "", , , , , ,    )



# 2. Pivot to long format for easier ggplot grouping
imp_long <- imp_data %>%
  rename(MDA = MeanDecreaseAccuracy, Gini = MeanDecreaseGini) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(MDA, Gini), names_to = "Metric", values_to = "Importance")

# 3. Create a faceted horizontal lollipop/dot plot
ggplot(imp_long, aes(x = reorder(Variable, Importance), y = Importance)) +
  geom_segment(aes(xend = Variable, yend = 0), color = "gray70", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(color = "#2c3e50", size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~Metric, scales = "free_x") +   # Gives each statistic its own dynamic axis
  coord_flip() +                             # Flips to horizontal for readable text labels
  labs(
    title = "Random Forest Variable Importance",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Importance Metric Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
    panel.spacing = unit(2, "lines")
  )

```

**Ordinal Regression on eGFR ranges**

The outcome variable 
```{r}
m <- polr(eGFR_range ~ AGE + alcohol_quantity * SEX_factor + ALC_freq_3 + Beer + Wine + Spirits_Liqueurs + Cider + Cocktails, data = ckd_filter, Hess=TRUE)

```

```{r}
summary(m)
(ctable <- coef(summary(m)))
p <- pnorm(abs(ctable[, "t value"]), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2
(ctable <- cbind(ctable, "p value" = p))
(ci <- confint(m))
confint.default(m)
```
For AGE, we would say that for a one unit increase in AGE (i.e., going from 0 to 1), we expect a
9.8e-02 decrease in the expected value of EGFR on the log odds scale, given all of the other variables in
the model are held constant.

```{r}
exp(cbind(OR = coef(m), ci))
```
